Record Class SkillDefinition

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
tech.kayys.wayang.agent.skill.SkillDefinition
Record Components:
id - Unique skill identifier, e.g. "coder", "security-keycloak-expert"
name - Human-readable display name
description - When to use this agent / skill
category - One of: "built-in", "template", "custom"
systemPrompt - The main persona / system instructions
subSkillPrompts - Task-type-specific prompts, e.g. {"GENERATE": "...", "REVIEW": "..."}
userPromptTemplate - Template for rendering user prompts; supports {{instruction}}, {{context}} placeholders
temperature - Default inference temperature
maxTokens - Default max tokens
defaultProvider - Default LLM provider ID
fallbackProvider - Fallback LLM provider ID
tools - Tool IDs this agent is allowed to use
orchestration - Orchestration config (only for orchestrator-type skills)
metadata - Additional properties: color, icon, tags, version, author, etc.
public record SkillDefinition(String id, String name, String description, String category, String systemPrompt, Map<String,String> subSkillPrompts, String userPromptTemplate, Double temperature, Integer maxTokens, String defaultProvider, String fallbackProvider, List<String> tools, SkillDefinition.OrchestrationConfig orchestration, Map<String,Object> metadata) extends Record
Skill Definition — the data-driven replacement for hardcoded agent executor classes.

A skill captures everything that makes an agent unique: its persona (system prompt), sub-skill prompts for different task types, inference parameters, tool access, and metadata.

Skills can be:

  • built-in — shipped as classpath resources (coder, planner, analytics, etc.)
  • template — pre-defined templates users can customize
  • custom — user-created via the UI canvas

On the UI canvas, users drag an "Agent" node and assign a skill (or create a new one). The unified SkillBasedAgentExecutor reads the skill definition at runtime and uses it to drive inference — no new Java code needed.
